title: SGLang update_weights_from_disk -- T1059 torch.load weights_only=False fallback enables pickle RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-15976 (GHSA-wf98-gv64-5wrf,
CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL), affecting SGLang.

`/update_weights_from_disk` loads model weight files
(`.bin`) that a caller can direct SGLang to fetch from a HuggingFace
repository. When loading, SGLang falls back to
`torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` -- PyTorch's own documentation
is explicit that this mode is UNSAFE for untrusted input, since it
enables full pickle deserialization rather than the restricted
tensor-only loading `weights_only=True` provides. A `.bin` file crafted
as a malicious pickle stream (disguised as model weights) therefore
achieves remote code execution the moment SGLang loads it -- the third
distinct pickle-deserialization RCE in the same coordinated disclosure
series alongside `observed_sglang_lora_adapter_safeunpickler_bypass_rce_t1059`
and `observed_sglang_dumper_subsystem_sandbox_escape_t1059`, this one
reached via a HuggingFace-repository weight-loading path rather than a
direct tensor-upload or debug-port path.

Detection logic flags a request to `/update_weights_from_disk` (or
`/update_weights_from_huggingface`, the equivalent repository-source
path) whose target file has a `.bin` extension and originates from a
repository outside an operator-curated allowlist -- the specific
artifact-loading path this bug reaches, distinct from the
already-trusted, operator-provisioned model repository.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (SGLang's own GHSA advisory + an
independent security researcher's corroborating disclosure write-up,
part of the same coordinated multi-CVE SGLang research series), no
patched version confirmed in the summary available at authoring time.
